title: The five rules
summary: What we agreed on 17 October. Two minutes.

config.body:
## Five rules for shared work

One person can serve four projects. These five sentences decide what happens when that collides.

| Rule | The question it answers |
| --- | --- |
| **People management** | Who owns this person’s workload, development and performance conversation |
| **Project authority** | What a project lead may assign, approve and change on their own |
| **Priority resolution** | Who decides when two leads need the same person at the same time |
| **Capacity change** | What existing work is named and moved when urgent work is added |
| **Visible work** | Where everyone can see agreed commitments and blockers |

## Why it matters now

Your executive team set four strategic objectives for 2027. The second is **execution efficiency, from 55% to 85%**. These five rules are how that number moves. They are provisional until 14 November, when the executive team decides what becomes permanent — and they will decide using what you log.

A rule only exists if it settles something. That is what we are testing.

title: Why people underperform
summary: The four blockers, and the Heart and Head quadrant. Keep this open.

config.body:
## Find out why before you decide what

Four things stop someone performing. Only one of them is attitude.

- **Psychological** — they do not believe they can do it, or do not believe it is safe to try and fail.

- **Emotional** — something is going on, here or at home, and it is using the capacity the work needs.

- **Environmental** — tools, information, access, time, or four projects and no priority rule. Not their fault.

- **Behavioural** — they can, they are able to, and they are choosing not to. The rarest of the four.

Most managers correct the fourth when the cause was the third.

## Heart and Head

| | What it means | What it asks of you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Heart high, Head high** | Willing and able | Stretch, motivate, promote — before someone else does |
| **Heart high, Head low** | Willing, not yet able | Train, and recognise the effort while they learn |
| **Heart low, Head high** | Able, not willing | Inspect. Something happened. Usually hurt, not defiance — find out before you act |
| **Heart low, Head low** | Neither | Exit, properly: a documented process, with HR from the start, never decided in frustration and never alone |

## Two rules for using this

Nobody sits permanently in a box. People move between them, and your behaviour is often what moves them.

Before you place anyone bottom-left, check two things: was there an environmental blocker, and was the standard ever actually stated to them? Most people who look bottom-left are top-left with an expectation nobody told them.

## Between now and 14 November

| What | By |
| --- | --- |
| Kill the meeting you named, and book the one-to-ones that replace it | Mon 2 Nov |
| Keep logging clashes as they happen — same four fields | Ongoing |
| Finish and agree every development plan with the person it is about | Fri 6 Nov |
| Have the performance conversation you worked on today | Fri 13 Nov |
| Say your team’s one-sentence direction to your team. Twice. | Ongoing |

## The four blockers, to keep handy

Psychological — they do not believe they can.  Emotional — something else is using the capacity.  Environmental — tools, time, information, or no priority rule.  Behavioural — they are choosing not to.

## The five coaching questions

1. What are you trying to get to?  2. What have you tried so far?  3. What is actually in the way?  4. What will you do about it this week?  5. **What do you need from me?**

Ask the fifth one in every one-to-one, and write the answer down in front of them.

## What happens on 14 November

Your executive team reviews the clash log and the 2026 business review, and decides which of the five rules becomes permanent. What you log before then is what they will be reading.

If you want to talk through a specific person before then, ask for a coaching slot. Thirty minutes, confidential.
